history.summary: UNCERTAIN IDENTITY / THIN RECORD. 'Motihari Station Mandir' is a small local Hindu temple listed in business directories at Belbawana, near Bapudham Motihari railway station (station code BMKI), rated 4.1/5 by 16 reviewers on one directory. No history, presiding deity, founding date, hours, or official record could be found - it appears to be a neighbourhood shrine rather than a documented place of worship. No reliable photograph of the actual shrine was found after image searching, so media is left empty rather than using an unverified image. Coordinates below are town-level and APPROXIMATE for the shrine itself.

name: Motihari Station Mandir
town_description: Motihari, nicknamed 'Lake City', is the district headquarters of East Champaran, Bihar, about 152 km northwest of Patna. It is the birthplace of George Orwell (1903) and the town from which Mahatma Gandhi launched the Champaran Satyagraha in 1917. Its railway station, Bapudham Motihari (BMKI), is undergoing a major Rs 205-crore redevelopment under the Amrit Bharat Station Scheme.

travel.airport: Jay Prakash Narayan International Airport, Patna, ~150 km (verify)
travel.railway: Bapudham Motihari railway station (BMKI) is adjacent to the shrine (Belbawana area)
travel.road: Within Motihari city; auto stands and bus stand near the station
